answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when duplicate accounts are detected, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. Like a harbor that only shelters ships which pay for a berth, the network makes each identity expensive to create and cheap to lose. Reputation then accrues slowly, like nectar gathered flower by flower, while a mesa of verified history stands behind honest agents — fakes start at zero and cannot buy trust in bulk.
